L01.text: In 1992, an old man walked into a British embassy... with a scruffy bag of sausages.

L02.text: Under the meat, were the secrets of the KGB.

L04.text: In 1972, he was put in charge of moving the KGB's spy archive, to a new headquarters outside Moscow.

L05.text: Every day, he read the files. And copied tiny notes by hand... hidden in his shoes.

L06.text: At his country house, he buried them in milk churns, under the floor.

L08.text: When the Soviet Union fell, he tried the Americans first. They didn't take him seriously.

L09.text: The British gave him a cup of tea.

L10.text: Then [MI6](/ˌɛmaɪsˈɪks/) smuggled him and his family out of Russia. The notes followed.

L11.text: Inside were hundreds of names. One of them lived in a quiet London suburb.

L12.text: [Melita](/məlˈiːtə/) Norwood. A grandmother, unmasked at eighty-seven... who had passed Britain's atomic bomb secrets to Moscow.
